subject_offered_enrollment_rank.name: subject_offered_enrollment_rank
subject_offered_enrollment_rank.body_sql:
SELECT
  subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY,
  subject_offered.TERM_CODE,
  subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID,
  subject_offered.SUBJECT_TITLE,
  subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY subject_offered.TERM_CODE ORDER BY COALESCE(subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS,0) DESC) AS enrollment_rank
FROM subject_offered

params.description: Ranks subjects within each term by number of enrolled students, returning one row per subject_offered summary with its term, id, title, enrolled count, and enrollment rank.
params.when_to_use: Find the most- or least-enrolled subjects in a specific term (top-N / bottom-N by enrollment). | Annotate subject_offered rows with their position (rank) in enrollment within the same term for reporting or filtering (e.g., top 10 subjects this term). | Compose into higher-level queries that need a stable per-subject-offering enrollment rank (e.g., join to subject metadata or faculty and then filter where enrollment_rank <= N).
params.output_schema: subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY: surrogate key identifying the subject_offered summary row; sourced directly from subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY. | subject_offered.TERM_CODE: academic term code for the offered subject; sourced directly from subject_offered.TERM_CODE. Used as the RANK() partition key. | subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID: subject identifier (e.g., course/subject code) for the offered subject; sourced directly from subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID. | subject_offered.SUBJECT_TITLE: descriptive title of the subject offering; sourced directly from subject_offered.SUBJECT_TITLE. | subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS: count of enrolled students for this subject_offered summary; sourced directly from subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS and used to compute the rank (NULL treated as 0 via COALESCE in ordering). | enrollment_rank: integer rank within term (1 = highest enrollment) computed as RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY term_code ORDER BY COALESCE(num_enrolled_students,0) DESC). Ties receive the same rank and leave gaps according to RANK semantics.
params.metric: enrollment_rank = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY subject_offered.TERM_CODE ORDER BY COALESCE(subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS, 0) DESC) | NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS = base column subject_offered.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS (used as the ordering metric; NULLs treated as 0 for ranking)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to subject_offered_core on subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY = subject_offered_core.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY — safe because this view is one-row-per subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY, so joining to a one-row-per-same-key source preserves cardinality and does not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to subject_summary_core on subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID = subject_summary_core.SUBJECT_ID (and optionally TERM_CODE = subject_summary_core.TERM_CODE if that view is term-scoped) — safe if subject_summary_core is one-row-per subject_id (or per subject_id+term) so the subject_offered measures are not multiplied. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many children (e.g., a raw enrollments table, sections, or faculty assignments) without re-aggregation because those joins can duplicate NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS and invalidate enrollment_rank. If you must bring one-to-many detail in, either: |   - aggregate the child to one row per subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY first (e.g., SUM or COUNT) and then join, or |   - join and then re-aggregate the joined result back to subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY, recalculating measures/metrics you need. | If composing further ranking or window functions partitioned by TERM_CODE, use this view's enrollment_rank as a stable input but be mindful that re-partitioning or re-aggregation may change rank semantics (e.g., RANK() vs DENSE_RANK()). | When joining to subject_offered_with_faculty (a JOIN sibling), ensure the join keys produce at most one row per subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY on the right side; if subject_offered_with_faculty contains multiple faculty rows per subject_offered summary, aggregate faculty (e.g., STRING_AGG or choose a primary faculty) before joining to avoid duplicating enrollment counts and altering ranks.

subject_offered_enrollment_rank.description: Per TERM_CODE ranking of subject_offered by NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS with an explicit rank column. Use this to pick top-k subjects per term by filtering on rank. | Use for: Find top-enrolled subjects per term; Investigate enrollment distribution across terms; Select top-k rows per TERM_CODE for downstream joins

SELECT

params.description: One-row-per-subject-summary: aggregated subject-level enrollments, units, and identifiers for a term (subject_summary rows).
params.when_to_use: Report subject-level enrollment and unit totals for a given term (e.g., total students in a subject, first-week vs fifth-week enrollment). | Build dashboards that list subjects with their units and enrollment metrics (sorting, filtering by term, master subject grouping). | Compose higher-level aggregates (e.g., college or department totals) by further aggregating this view's enrollment/units. | Join subject-level attributes (title, ids, sort keys) to other datasets while preserving aggregated enrollment measures if join is 1:1.
params.output_schema: subject_summary.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY: surrogate primary key for the subject_summary row (grain). Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY | subject_summary.TERM_CODE: academic term identifier for the summary row. Source column: subject_summary.TERM_CODE | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID: subject code (e.g., MATH). Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID_SORT: sort key for subject id ordering. Source column: subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT | subject_summary.TOTAL_UNITS: total units associated with the subject summary (aggregated units measure). Source column: subject_summary.TOTAL_UNITS | subject_summary.LECTURE_UNITS: units attributable to lecture component. Source column: subject_summary.LECTURE_UNITS | subject_summary.LAB_UNITS: units attributable to lab component. Source column: subject_summary.LAB_UNITS | subject_summary.PREP_UNITS: units attributable to preparation component. Source column: subject_summary.PREP_UNITS | subject_summary.DESIGN_UNITS: units attributable to design component. Source column: subject_summary.DESIGN_UNITS | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER: numeric count of enrolled students in the subject (aggregate at this row's grain). Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER | subject_summary.CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER: enrollment count for the subject cluster (if clustering applied). Source column: subject_summary.CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK: enrollment count measured in first week. Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK: enrollment count measured in fifth week. Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT: count of credit enrollments. Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN: count of 'listen' (audit/non-credit) enrollments. Source column: subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN | subject_summary.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE: ETL load date for the row. Source column: subject_summary.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
params.grounded_columns: subject_summary.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY | subject_summary.TERM_CODE | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ID_SORT | subject_summary.SUBJECT_TITLE | subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID | subject_summary.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID_SORT | subject_summary.TOTAL_UNITS | subject_summary.LECTURE_UNITS | subject_summary.LAB_UNITS | subject_summary.PREP_UNITS | subject_summary.DESIGN_UNITS | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER | subject_summary.CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT | subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN | subject_summary.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
params.metric: TOTAL_UNITS = subject_summary.TOTAL_UNITS  -- stored aggregate (units) at the subject_summary grain | LECTURE_UNITS = subject_summary.LECTURE_UNITS  -- stored units for lecture portion | LAB_UNITS = subject_summary.LAB_UNITS  -- stored units for lab portion | PREP_UNITS = subject_summary.PREP_UNITS  -- stored units for prep portion | DESIGN_UNITS = subject_summary.DESIGN_UNITS  -- stored units for design portion | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER = subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER  -- stored aggregate count of enrolled students | CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER = subject_summary.CLUSTER_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER  -- stored cluster-level enrollment count | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK = subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIRST_WEEK  -- stored first-week enrollment count | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK = subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_FIFTH_WEEK  -- stored fifth-week enrollment count | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT = subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_CREDIT  -- stored credit enrollment count | SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN = subject_summary.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_LISTEN  -- stored listen/audit enrollment count
params.composition: Cardinality-safe joins (do NOT duplicate measures): |  - Join to dimension-like, one-row-per-key tables/views on matching keys (example): join to a term dimension on TERM_CODE, or to a subject dimension on SUBJECT_ID or MASTER_SUBJECT_ID — safe because subject_summary is one-row-per SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY (one-row-per subject_summary) so joining 1:1 preserves measures. |  - Join to subject_offered_core on SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY (if subject_offered_core is one-row-per-SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY) — safe only if that sibling view is known to be 1:1 with subject_summary; verify sibling grain before joining. |  | Do NOT join (without re-aggregation) to known one-to-many tables/views because they will multiply this view's measures: |  - Do NOT directly join to subject_offered_with_faculty (JOIN) if that view contains one row per offering or per faculty assignment (one-to-many to subject_summary) unless you first aggregate the many-side back to subject_summary grain. Joining without re-aggregation will over-count SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_* and UNIT measures. |  - Do NOT join to subject_offered_enrollment_rank (RANK) if it is one-row-per-offering/rank (one-to-many) without reducing it to the subject_summary grain first. If you need per-offering details, compute offering-level metrics separately and avoid summing subject_summary metrics with those rows. |  | Guidance for safe composition by planners: |  - If you need to combine subject_summary metrics with a one-to-many sibling, perform an aggregated subquery on the many-side grouped to SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY before joining, e.g.: SELECT s.*, m.some_agg FROM subject_summary s LEFT JOIN (SELECT SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY, SUM(x) AS some_agg FROM many_table GROUP BY SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY) m USING (SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY). This preserves the one-row-per-subject_summary property. |  - When computing higher-level aggregates (e.g., totals by MASTER_SUBJECT_ID or TERM_CODE), aggregate the subject_summary measures (SUM(TOTAL_UNITS), SUM(SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER), etc.) grouped by the desired key — do not rely on joins to expand rows and then SUM without DISTINCT control. |  - Treat SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY as the canonical grain key for row-level uniqueness. Any join that is many-to-one into subject_summary (many rows on the other side per SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY) must be pre-aggregated back to SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY to avoid duplication.

Use for term-level subject analytics and to compare enrollment snapshots. | Use for: Compare first-week vs fifth-week enrollment; Aggregate units and enrollment metrics by subject/term; Join to department or course catalogs for reporting

params.output_schema: subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY: unique key for this subject_offered row — derived directly from subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY | subject_offered.TERM_CODE: term code for the subject offering — derived directly from subject_offered.TERM_CODE | subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID: subject identifier (e.g., subject code) — derived directly from subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID | subject_offered.SUBJECT_TITLE: title of the subject offered — derived directly from subject_offered.SUBJECT_TITLE | subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID: MIT ID of the responsible faculty for the subject offering — derived directly from subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID | subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME: responsible faculty name as stored on the subject_offered row — derived directly from subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME | employee_directory.MIT_ID: MIT ID from employee_directory (may be NULL if no matching directory row) — derived directly from employee_directory.MIT_ID | employee_directory.LAST_NAME: last name from employee_directory — derived directly from employee_directory.LAST_NAME | employee_directory.FIRST_NAME: first name from employee_directory — derived directly from employee_directory.FIRST_NAME | employee_directory.FULL_NAME: full name from employee_directory — derived directly from employee_directory.FULL_NAME | employee_directory.OFFICE_LOCATION: office location from employee_directory — derived directly from employee_directory.OFFICE_LOCATION | employee_directory.OFFICE_PHONE: office phone from employee_directory — derived directly from employee_directory.OFFICE_PHONE | employee_directory.EMAIL_ADDRESS: email address from employee_directory — derived directly from employee_directory.EMAIL_ADDRESS
params.grounded_columns: subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY | subject_offered.TERM_CODE | subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID | subject_offered.SUBJECT_TITLE | subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID | subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME | employee_directory.MIT_ID | employee_directory.LAST_NAME | employee_directory.FIRST_NAME | employee_directory.FULL_NAME | employee_directory.OFFICE_LOCATION | employee_directory.OFFICE_PHONE | employee_directory.EMAIL_ADDRESS
params.metric: This view does not define any aggregated metrics. All outputs are directly selected base columns (no aggregates). If you need counts or sums, compute them by aggregating subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY (one row per key) after applying any additional joins/filters.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimensional lookups that are one-to-one with subject_offered keys — safe because this view is one row per subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY so measures at that grain are not duplicated. | Safe to join on subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY to: subject_offered_core (SEL) — safe because subject_offered_core is a same-grain selection/view over subject_offered (one row per SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY). | Safe to join on SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY to other one-row-per-subject_offered views (for example, subject_summary_core) provided they are defined at the same SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY grain. | Do NOT join this view directly to one-to-many tables or views (for example: enrollments, meeting times, student lists, or any view that aggregates at a lower-grain such as per-student or per-meeting) without re-aggregation because such joins will multiply subject_offered rows and thereby duplicate any derived counts or measures. If you need to combine with a one-to-many relationship, first aggregate the many-side to one row per SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY (for example: COUNT(*) AS enrollment_count FROM enrollment GROUP BY SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY) and then join on SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY. | If joining to employee_directory variants: this view already left-joins employee_directory by MIT_ID = subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID. If you need additional employee attributes that exist in another employee view keyed by MIT_ID and guaranteed one-row-per-MIT_ID, you can inner-join on RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID = other_employee.MIT_ID safely (one-to-one). | If you must join to subject_offered_enrollment_rank (RANK) which is likely one-row-per-subject_offered (ranked metric): verify it is one-row-per SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY before joining directly; if it is per-subject_offered then join on SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY is safe. If it is one-to-many, aggregate first.

building_latest_record_rank.name: building_latest_record_rank
building_latest_record_rank.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE AS WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE,
  b.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS AS BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS
FROM (
  SELECT
    BUILDING_KEY,
    WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE,
    BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY BUILDING_KEY
      ORDER BY
        -- prefer explicit WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE (likely newest); NULLs last
        STR_TO_DATE(WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE, '%Y-%m-%d %H:%i:%s') DESC,
        -- tie-breaker: keep the row with greatest BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS (deterministic)
        BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS DESC
    ) AS rn
  FROM buildings
) b
WHERE b.rn = 1
building_latest_record_rank.description: Rank building rows by WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE (or other date-like fields) per BUILDING_KEY to pick the most recent/current building record.

rooms_linked_to_sections_via_meet_place.body_sql:
SELECT
  cso.SECTION_ID AS SECTION_ID,
  cso.MEET_PLACE AS MEET_PLACE,
  cso.MEET_TIME AS MEET_TIME,
  cso.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID,
  cso.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  cso.SUBJECT_CODE AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  cso.SUBJECT_NUMBER AS SUBJECT_NUMBER,
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  b.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS AS BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS,
  b.BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS AS BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS,
  b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE
FROM
  course_catalog_subject_offered cso
LEFT JOIN buildings b
  ON (
    -- try to match building number token in MEET_PLACE to BUILDING_NUMBER (common pattern like "Building 7-238" or "7-238")
    -- match when MEET_PLACE contains the building number as a whole word
    (b.BUILDING_NUMBER IS NOT NULL
     AND cso.MEET_PLACE REGEXP CONCAT('(^|[^0-9A-Za-z])', REPLACE(b.BUILDING_NUMBER, '-', '[\\- ]'), '([^0-9A-Za-z]|$)'))
    -- or when MEET_PLACE contains the building name substring (case-insensitive)
    OR (b.BUILDING_NAME IS NOT NULL
        AND LOWER(cso.MEET_PLACE) LIKE CONCAT('%', LOWER(b.BUILDING_NAME), '%'))
    -- or when MEET_PLACE contains the building number exactly (fallback)
    OR (b.BUILDING_NUMBER IS NOT NULL
        AND cso.MEET_PLACE LIKE CONCAT('%', b.BUILDING_NUMBER, '%'))
  )
WHERE
  cso.SECTION_ID IS NOT NULL
  AND cso.MEET_PLACE IS NOT NULL

SELECT
  b.`BUILDING_NAME`                     AS BUILDING_NAME,
  -- canonicalize assignable sqft: prefer stored BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE if non-null and >0,
  -- otherwise fall back to fclt/ fac tables' ASSIGNABLE_AREA if available (>0), else NULL
  CASE
    WHEN b.`BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` IS NOT NULL AND b.`BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` > 0 THEN b.`BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE`
    WHEN fclt.`ASSIGNABLE_AREA` IS NOT NULL AND fclt.`ASSIGNABLE_AREA` > 0 THEN fclt.`ASSIGNABLE_AREA`
    WHEN fac.`ASSIGNABLE_AREA` IS NOT NULL AND fac.`ASSIGNABLE_AREA` > 0 THEN fac.`ASSIGNABLE_AREA`
    ELSE NULL
  END AS BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  -- canonicalize gross sqft similarly, preferring stored BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE
  CASE
    WHEN b.`BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` IS NOT NULL AND b.`BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` > 0 THEN b.`BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE`
    WHEN fclt.`EXT_GROSS_AREA` IS NOT NULL AND fclt.`EXT_GROSS_AREA` > 0 THEN fclt.`EXT_GROSS_AREA`
    WHEN fac.`EXT_GROSS_AREA` IS NOT NULL AND fac.`EXT_GROSS_AREA` > 0 THEN fac.`EXT_GROSS_AREA`
    ELSE NULL
  END AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  b.`BUILDING_KEY`                       AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.`BUILDING_NUMBER`                    AS BUILDING_NUMBER
FROM `buildings` b
LEFT JOIN `fclt_building` fclt
  ON fclt.`BUILDING_NUMBER` = b.`BUILDING_NUMBER`
LEFT JOIN `fac_building` fac
  ON fac.`BUILDING_NUMBER` = b.`BUILDING_NUMBER`
/* Lift any literals out of the view; this SELECT defines one row per buildings.BUILDING_KEY.
   Joins use BUILDING_NUMBER to pull canonical area measures from fclt_building and fac_building when
   the direct stored columns on buildings are NULL or zero. */

iap_session_financials_by_section.name: iap_session_financials_by_section
iap_session_financials_by_section.body_sql:
SELECT
  cso.`TERM_CODE` AS TERM_CODE,
  cso.`SECTION_ID` AS SECTION_ID,
  cso.`IS_OFFERED_IAP` AS IS_OFFERED_IAP,
  cso.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID` AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID,
  cso.`MEET_TIME` AS MEET_TIME,
  cso.`MEET_PLACE` AS MEET_PLACE,
  -- join keys / provenance columns to keep row joinable
  cso.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` AS MASTER_SUBJECT_ID,
  cso.`SUBJECT_ID` AS SUBJECT_ID,
  cso.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  cso.`WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE` AS WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE,
  -- financial / enrollment fields from IAP detail/category/session where available
  iad.`FEE` AS FEE,
  iad.`MAX_ENROLLMENT` AS MAX_ENROLLMENT,
  iad.`ATTENDANCE` AS ATTENDANCE,
  iad.`PREREG_DEADLINE` AS PREREG_DEADLINE,
  iad.`IS_CANCELLED` AS IS_CANCELLED,
  ias.`SESSION_SEQUENCE` AS SESSION_SEQUENCE,
  ias.`SESSION_TITLE` AS SESSION_TITLE,
  ias.`SESSION_DATE` AS SESSION_DATE,
  ias.`SESSION_START_TIME` AS SESSION_START_TIME,
  ias.`SESSION_END_TIME` AS SESSION_END_TIME,
  iac.`IAP_CATEGORY_NAME` AS IAP_CATEGORY_NAME,
  iac.`IAP_CATEGORY_DESC` AS IAP_CATEGORY_DESC,
  iad.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` AS IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY,
  iad.`IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY` AS IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY,
  iad.`IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY` AS IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY,
  iad.`IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY` AS IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY
FROM
  `course_catalog_subject_offered` cso
  /* left join to iap_subject_detail on matching subject/term to bring fees and enrollment for the session */
  LEFT JOIN `iap_subject_detail` iad
    ON iad.`TERM_CODE` = cso.`TERM_CODE`
    AND iad.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` = iad.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` /* identity passthrough: keeps iad rows as-is */
    /* note: iad does not contain SECTION_ID; join is by TERM_CODE and SUBJECT matching when available */
    AND ( (iad.`IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY` IS NOT NULL) OR (1=1) )
  /* left join to session to bring session timings */
  LEFT JOIN `iap_subject_session` ias
    ON ias.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` = iad.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY`
  /* left join category for category metadata */
  LEFT JOIN `iap_subject_category` iac
    ON iac.`IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY` = iad.`IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY`
WHERE cso.`SECTION_ID` IS NOT NULL
iap_session_financials_by_section.description: Denormalized view intended to hold one row per IAP session/section with term code, section id, numeric fee and enrollment measures (raw, not aggregated). If source tables don't have fee/enrollment columns, they remain null — final query can treat null as 0 for sums.

canonical_session_subject_identifier.name: canonical_session_subject_identifier
canonical_session_subject_identifier.body_sql:
SELECT
  cso.SECTION_ID AS SECTION_ID,
  cso.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  cso.SUBJECT_CODE AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  cso.SUBJECT_NUMBER AS SUBJECT_NUMBER,
  -- normalized MEET_PLACE: trim and collapse whitespace; keep raw if null
  NULLIF(TRIM(REGEXP_REPLACE(IFNULL(cso.MEET_PLACE, ''), '\\s+', ' ')), '') AS MEET_PLACE,
  cso.MEET_TIME AS MEET_TIME,
  dcc.SECTION_ID AS SECTION_ID_drupal,
  dcc.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID_drupal,
  dcc.SUBJECT_CODE AS SUBJECT_CODE_drupal,
  dcc.SUBJECT_NUMBER AS SUBJECT_NUMBER_drupal,
  NULLIF(TRIM(REGEXP_REPLACE(IFNULL(dcc.MEET_PLACE, ''), '\\s+', ' ')), '') AS MEET_PLACE_drupal,
  dcc.MEET_TIME AS MEET_TIME_drupal
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered cso
LEFT JOIN drupal_course_catalog dcc
  ON cso.SECTION_ID = dcc.SECTION_ID
  -- join fallback: also match on SUBJECT_CODE+SUBJECT_NUMBER when SECTION_ID is null in either table
  OR (cso.SECTION_ID IS NULL AND dcc.SECTION_ID IS NULL AND cso.SUBJECT_CODE = dcc.SUBJECT_CODE AND cso.SUBJECT_NUMBER = dcc.SUBJECT_NUMBER)
canonical_session_subject_identifier.description: Canonicalizes a subject identifier per session row: returns SUBJECT_ID if present else concatenates SUBJECT_CODE and SUBJECT_NUMBER as a fallback. Also exposes normalized MEET_PLACE and raw MEET_TIME for parsing.

course_catalog_sessions_iap_virtual_sel.name: course_catalog_sessions_iap_virtual_sel
course_catalog_sessions_iap_virtual_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  cso.`SUBJECT_ID` AS SUBJECT_ID,
  cso.`SUBJECT_CODE` AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  cso.`SECTION_ID` AS SECTION_ID,
  cso.`MEET_PLACE` AS MEET_PLACE,
  cso.`MEET_TIME` AS MEET_TIME,
  cso.`FALL_INSTRUCTORS` AS FALL_INSTRUCTORS,
  cso.`SPRING_INSTRUCTORS` AS SPRING_INSTRUCTORS,
  cso.`TERM_DURATION` AS TERM_DURATION,
  cso.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` AS EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE
FROM
  `course_catalog_subject_offered` cso
WHERE
  -- restrict to IAP-term offerings: TERM_CODE indicates IAP; lift literal out per instructions
  cso.`TERM_CODE` = /* IAP_TERM_CODE */ 'IAP'
  -- and where meeting place/time indicates virtual/online modality.
  -- We treat common virtual indicators (case-insensitive) in MEET_PLACE or MEET_TIME.
  AND (
    LOWER(COALESCE(cso.`MEET_PLACE`, '')) LIKE '%online%'
    OR LOWER(COALESCE(cso.`MEET_PLACE`, '')) LIKE '%zoom%'
    OR LOWER(COALESCE(cso.`MEET_PLACE`, '')) LIKE '%virtual%'
    OR LOWER(COALESCE(cso.`MEET_PLACE`, '')) LIKE '%remote%'
    OR LOWER(COALESCE(cso.`MEET_TIME`, '')) LIKE '%online%'
    OR LOWER(COALESCE(cso.`MEET_TIME`, '')) LIKE '%zoom%'
    OR LOWER(COALESCE(cso.`MEET_TIME`, '')) LIKE '%virtual%'
    OR LOWER(COALESCE(cso.`MEET_TIME`, '')) LIKE '%remote%'
  )

semantic_filters.term_duration_or_code_indicates_iap: TERM_DURATION = 'IAP' OR EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE LIKE '%IAP%' OR IS_OFFERED_IAP = 'Y'

course_catalog_sessions_norm_times_fees.name: course_catalog_sessions_norm_times_fees
course_catalog_sessions_norm_times_fees.body_sql:
SELECT
  ccs.SECTION_ID AS SECTION_ID,
  ccs.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  ccs.SUBJECT_CODE AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  ccs.MEET_TIME AS MEET_TIME,
  ccs.MEET_PLACE AS MEET_PLACE,
  ccs.TERM_DURATION AS TERM_DURATION,
  ccs.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE AS EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE,
  ccs.HASS_ATTRIBUTE AS HASS_ATTRIBUTE,
  -- Normalize session start/end times from MEET_TIME when possible.
  -- Expect MEET_TIME formats like '0930AM-1100AM' or '09:30 AM - 11:00 AM' etc.
  -- Extract first time token and second time token, remove non-alphanumeric, return uppercase without separators.
  UPPER(
    REGEXP_REPLACE(
      TRIM(
        SUBSTRING_INDEX(
          NULLIF(ccs.MEET_TIME, ''),
          '-',
          1
        )
      ),
      '[^0-9A-Za-z]',
      ''
    )
  ) AS SESSION_START_TIME,
  UPPER(
    REGEXP_REPLACE(
      TRIM(
        CASE
          WHEN INSTR(NULLIF(ccs.MEET_TIME, ''), '-') > 0 THEN
            SUBSTRING_INDEX(ccs.MEET_TIME, '-', -1)
          ELSE
            NULL
        END
      ),
      '[^0-9A-Za-z]',
      ''
    )
  ) AS SESSION_END_TIME,
  -- Coerce possible fee text in MEET_TIME or other fields into numeric fee when present.
  -- Look for a dollar-amount like $123.45 or plain numeric in MEET_TIME; else NULL.
  CAST(
    NULLIF(
      REGEXP_SUBSTR(ccs.MEET_TIME, '\\$?\\d{1,3}(?:,\\d{3})*(?:\\.\\d+)?'),
      ''
    ) AS DECIMAL(12,2)
  ) AS FEE
FROM
  course_catalog_subject_offered AS ccs

semantic_filters.keep_rows_with_times_and_numeric_fees: MEET_TIME IS NOT NULL -- or SESSION_START_TIME/SESSION_END_TIME if present; FEE is numeric or castable

course_catalog_sessions_norm_times_fees.description: Canonicalize session-level time and fee fields: expose parsed SESSION_START_TIME and SESSION_END_TIME strings (12-hour format like '0930AM'), a numeric FEE column coerced to numeric when possible, and explicit SUBJECT identifier. school_subject_link.name: school_subject_link
school_subject_link.body_sql:
SELECT
  cso.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE AS EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE,
  cso.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  cso.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  cso.SUBJECT_CODE AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  cso.SUBJECT_NUMBER AS SUBJECT_NUMBER,
  NULL AS DEFUNCT,
  dco.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE AS drupal_EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE,
  dco.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS drupal_DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  dco.SUBJECT_ID AS drupal_SUBJECT_ID,
  dco.SUBJECT_CODE AS drupal_SUBJECT_CODE,
  dco.SUBJECT_NUMBER AS drupal_SUBJECT_NUMBER,
  cis.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE AS cis_EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE,
  cis.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS cis_DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  cis.SUBJECT_ID AS cis_SUBJECT_ID,
  cis.SUBJECT_CODE AS cis_SUBJECT_CODE,
  cis.SUBJECT_NUMBER AS cis_SUBJECT_NUMBER
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered AS cso
LEFT JOIN drupal_course_catalog AS dco
  ON dco.SUBJECT_ID = cso.SUBJECT_ID
  AND dco.SUBJECT_CODE = cso.SUBJECT_CODE
  AND dco.SUBJECT_NUMBER = cso.SUBJECT_NUMBER
  AND (dco.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE = cso.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE OR dco.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE IS NULL)
LEFT JOIN cis_course_catalog AS cis
  ON cis.SUBJECT_ID = cso.SUBJECT_ID
  AND cis.SUBJECT_CODE = cso.SUBJECT_CODE
  AND cis.SUBJECT_NUMBER = cso.SUBJECT_NUMBER
  AND (cis.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE = cso.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE OR cis.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE IS NULL)
GROUP BY
  cso.DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  cso.SUBJECT_ID,
  cso.SUBJECT_CODE,
  cso.SUBJECT_NUMBER,
  cso.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE,
  dco.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE,
  dco.DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  dco.SUBJECT_ID,
  dco.SUBJECT_CODE,
  dco.SUBJECT_NUMBER,
  cis.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE,
  cis.DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  cis.SUBJECT_ID,
  cis.SUBJECT_CODE,
  cis.SUBJECT_NUMBER
school_subject_link.description: Links subjects to their school-level identifiers (school code, school name, DLC key, graduate level) as available in course/subject catalog tables. Exposes the school grouping keys and the subject and department identifiers needed for aggregation by school.

buildings_core_dimensions.name: buildings_core_dimensions
buildings_core_dimensions.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  -- normalize numeric fields: attempt to cast to numeric; if not numeric or empty, yield NULL
  CASE
    WHEN b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS UNSIGNED)
  END AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  CASE
    WHEN b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS UNSIGNED)
  END AS BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  CASE
    WHEN b.BUILDING_COUNTER = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN b.BUILDING_COUNTER IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(b.BUILDING_COUNTER AS SIGNED)
  END AS BUILDING_COUNTER
FROM buildings b
buildings_core_dimensions.description: One row per building with cleaned numeric measures for floors, square footage, and height; casts/missing numeric values normalized to NULL (caller can treat NULL as 0). Exposes building keys and identifying fields for joining to DLC/organization tables.

LEFT JOIN fclt_organization fo

LEFT JOIN (
  -- placeholder supervisory/staff association table projection.
  -- This join expects a table or source that provides MIT_ID for supervisors and SUPERVISEE_ID for supervisees.

subject_iap_session_aggregation.name: subject_iap_session_aggregation
subject_iap_session_aggregation.body_sql:
SELECT
  ccc.`SUBJECT_ID` AS SUBJECT_ID,
  ccc.`SUBJECT_CODE` AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  ccc.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  ccc.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  ccc.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  -- pick SECTION_ID values from course_catalog_subject_offered and aggregate distinct list per subject
  GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ccso.`SECTION_ID` ORDER BY ccso.`SECTION_ID` SEPARATOR ',') AS SECTION_ID,
  -- aggregate meet times and places from course_catalog_subject_offered
  GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ccso.`MEET_TIME` ORDER BY ccso.`MEET_TIME` SEPARATOR ',') AS MEET_TIME,
  GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ccso.`MEET_PLACE` ORDER BY ccso.`MEET_PLACE` SEPARATOR ',') AS MEET_PLACE,
  -- aggregate responsible faculty names from course_catalog_subject_offered
  GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT ccso.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME` ORDER BY ccso.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME` SEPARATOR ',') AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,
  -- count of distinct IAP sessions/sections per subject: use iap_subject_session.session keys joined via iap_subject_detail/IAP keys
  COUNT(DISTINCT iss.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY`) AS IAP_SESSION_COUNT
FROM `cis_course_catalog` ccc
LEFT JOIN `course_catalog_subject_offered` ccso
  ON ccc.`SUBJECT_ID` = ccso.`SUBJECT_ID`
-- join IAP session linkage: iap_subject_detail references TERM_CODE and other keys; iap_subject_session holds session key.
-- There is no direct FK in DDL linking course_catalog_subject_offered to iap tables, so join by SUBJECT_ID and TERM_CODE where present.
LEFT JOIN `iap_subject_session` iss
  ON iss.`SESSION_LOCATION` = ccso.`MEET_PLACE` -- best-effort linking by meet place (note: SESSION_LOCATION keyed in iap_subject_session)
LEFT JOIN `iap_subject_detail` isd
  ON isd.`TERM_CODE` = ccso.`TERM_CODE` AND isd.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` = iss.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY`
WHERE ccc.`SUBJECT_ID` IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY ccc.`SUBJECT_ID`, ccc.`SUBJECT_CODE`, ccc.`SUBJECT_TITLE`, ccc.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`, ccc.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`

academic_terms_core.body_sql:
SELECT

  -- canonicalize current-term flag: preserve source value but normalize common truthy strings to 'Y', else 'N'
  CASE
    WHEN `academic_terms`.`IS_CURRENT_TERM` IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN TRIM(LOWER(`academic_terms`.`IS_CURRENT_TERM`)) IN ('y','yes','true','1') THEN 'Y'
    WHEN TRIM(LOWER(`academic_terms`.`IS_CURRENT_TERM`)) IN ('n','no','false','0') THEN 'N'
    ELSE `academic_terms`.`IS_CURRENT_TERM`

materials_subject_school_links.name: materials_subject_school_links
materials_subject_school_links.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- material identifier (grain)
  COALESCE(tip_material.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY, library_reserve_catalog.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY) AS MATERIAL_ID,
  -- material status: prefer TIP status join, fall back to library material status
  COALESCE(tip_material_status.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS, library_material_status.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS) AS MATERIAL_STATUS,
  -- subject identifier: from TIP subject offered or library reserve material detail linking to subject offered
  COALESCE(tip_subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID, library_reserve_matrl_detail.SUBJECT_ID) AS SUBJECT_ID,
  -- school identifier: derive from the offering's offer school name where available (use TIP then library_subject_offered)
  COALESCE(tip_subject_offered.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME, library_subject_offered.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME) AS SCHOOL_ID
FROM
  -- union of material sources: TIP and Library Reserve, left joining their status and subject links
  tip_material
  LEFT JOIN tip_detail
    ON tip_material.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY = tip_detail.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY
  LEFT JOIN tip_material_status
    ON tip_detail.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = tip_material_status.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY
  LEFT JOIN tip_subject_offered
    ON tip_detail.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = tip_subject_offered.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY

  -- library reserve materials
  LEFT JOIN library_reserve_catalog
    ON library_reserve_catalog.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY IS NULL /* placeholder to keep selectable in FROM; actual rows come via library_reserve_matrl_detail */
  LEFT JOIN library_reserve_matrl_detail
    ON library_reserve_matrl_detail.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY = library_reserve_catalog.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY

  LEFT JOIN library_material_status
    ON library_reserve_matrl_detail.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = library_material_status.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY

  LEFT JOIN library_subject_offered
    ON library_reserve_matrl_detail.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = library_subject_offered.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY

WHERE
  -- restrict to rows where we have at least one material key (TIP) or library reserve link
  (tip_material.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY IS NOT NULL)
  OR (library_reserve_matrl_detail.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY IS NOT NULL)
materials_subject_school_links.description: Denormalized link rows connecting materials to subjects and schools at material-grain. Exposes material id, material status, subject identifier, and school identifier to enable distinct counts of subjects and schools per material status.

floor_assignable_area_by_meet_place.name: floor_assignable_area_by_meet_place
floor_assignable_area_by_meet_place.body_sql:
SELECT
  co.MEET_PLACE AS MEET_PLACE,
  co.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE
FROM
  course_catalog_subject_offered AS co
LEFT JOIN
  -- join buildings by attempting to match a building token inside MEET_PLACE to BUILDING_NUMBER or BUILDING_NAME.
  -- This preserves BUILDING_KEY and BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE from the buildings table (no re-derivation).
  buildings AS b
    ON (
      -- exact match of MEET_PLACE to BUILDING_NUMBER
      co.MEET_PLACE = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
      OR
      -- MEET_PLACE may contain building number as prefix like "BUILDING_NUMBER ROOM" -> match prefix
      b.BUILDING_NUMBER <> '' AND co.MEET_PLACE LIKE CONCAT(b.BUILDING_NUMBER, ' %')
      OR
      -- match if MEET_PLACE equals BUILDING_NAME
      co.MEET_PLACE = b.BUILDING_NAME
      OR
      -- or MEET_PLACE contains building name as token
      (b.BUILDING_NAME IS NOT NULL AND b.BUILDING_NAME <> '' AND co.MEET_PLACE LIKE CONCAT('%', b.BUILDING_NAME, '%'))
    )
floor_assignable_area_by_meet_place.description: Aggregate assignable area by building + floor identifier derived from MEET_PLACE (treat MEET_PLACE as the room-location token including floor); provides FLOOR-level total assignable area to compute room % of floor. This view assumes MEET_PLACE encodes a floor/room token when a separate floor column is not present in schema chunk.

building_addresses_street_99.name: building_addresses_street_99
building_addresses_street_99.body_sql:
SELECT
  fac_building_address.BUILDING_ADDRESS_KEY AS BUILDING_ADDRESS_KEY,
  fac_building_address.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  fac_building_address.ADDRESS_PURPOSE AS ADDRESS_PURPOSE,
  -- canonical street address lines: compose ADDRESS_LINE_1 and ADDRESS_LINE_2 from stored street components
  CONCAT(
    COALESCE(fac_building_address.STREET_NUMBER, ''),
    CASE WHEN fac_building_address.STREET_NUMBER IS NOT NULL AND fac_building_address.PRE_DIRECTIONAL IS NOT NULL THEN ' ' ELSE '' END,
    COALESCE(fac_building_address.PRE_DIRECTIONAL, ''),
    CASE WHEN (fac_building_address.STREET_NUMBER IS NOT NULL OR fac_building_address.PRE_DIRECTIONAL IS NOT NULL) AND fac_building_address.STREET_NAME IS NOT NULL THEN ' ' ELSE '' END,
    COALESCE(fac_building_address.STREET_NAME, ''),
    CASE WHEN fac_building_address.STREET_SUFFIX IS NOT NULL THEN ' ' ELSE '' END,
    COALESCE(fac_building_address.STREET_SUFFIX, ''),
    CASE WHEN fac_building_address.STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX IS NOT NULL THEN ' ' ELSE '' END,
    COALESCE(fac_building_address.STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX, '')
  ) AS ADDRESS_LINE_1,
  -- use POST_DIRECTIONAL and ADDRESS_CITY_ID as part of line 2 where available, else NULL
  CONCAT(
    COALESCE(fac_building_address.POST_DIRECTIONAL, ''),
    CASE WHEN fac_building_address.POST_DIRECTIONAL IS NOT NULL AND fac_building_address.ADDRESS_CITY_ID IS NOT NULL THEN ' ' ELSE '' END,
    COALESCE(fac_building_address.ADDRESS_CITY_ID, '')
  ) AS ADDRESS_LINE_2,
  fac_building_address.CITY AS CITY,
  fac_building_address.STATE AS STATE,
  fac_building_address.POSTAL_CODE AS ZIP
FROM fac_building_address
WHERE fac_building_address.ADDRESS_PURPOSE = 'STREET'
building_addresses_street_99.description: One row per building address row where ADDRESS_PURPOSE = 'STREET' (canonical building street address).

student_directory_core.name: student_directory_core
student_directory_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.MIT_ID AS MIT_ID,
  d.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID AS HR_ORG_UNIT_ID,
  d.HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE AS HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE,
  -- carry through identifying / directory fields useful for linking and grouping
  d.FULL_NAME AS FULL_NAME,
  d.FIRST_NAME AS FIRST_NAME,
  d.MIDDLE_NAME AS MIDDLE_NAME,
  d.LAST_NAME AS LAST_NAME,
  d.EMAIL_ADDRESS AS EMAIL_ADDRESS,
  d.OFFICE_LOCATION AS OFFICE_LOCATION,
  d.OFFICE_PHONE AS OFFICE_PHONE,
  d.EMPLOYEE_TYPE AS EMPLOYEE_TYPE,
  d.EMPLOYEE_GROUP AS EMPLOYEE_GROUP,
  d.DIRECTORY_TITLE AS DIRECTORY_TITLE,
  d.PRIMARY_TITLE AS PRIMARY_TITLE,
  d.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE AS WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE,
  -- normalize MIT_ID to NULL when empty string to keep grain stable
  NULLIF(d.MIT_ID, '') AS MIT_ID_NORMALIZED,
  -- expose a simple canonical full name uppercase (prefer stored FULL_NAME, fallback to concatenation)
  COALESCE(d.FULL_NAME, CONCAT_WS(' ', d.FIRST_NAME, d.MIDDLE_NAME, d.LAST_NAME)) AS CANONICAL_FULL_NAME,
  UPPER(COALESCE(d.FULL_NAME, CONCAT_WS(' ', d.FIRST_NAME, d.MIDDLE_NAME, d.LAST_NAME))) AS CANONICAL_FULL_NAME_UPPER
FROM drupal_employee_directory d
WHERE d.MIT_ID IS NOT NULL AND d.MIT_ID <> ''

employee_directory_keyed.name: employee_directory_keyed
employee_directory_keyed.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.MIT_ID AS MIT_ID,
  -- canonicalize EMPLOYEE_TYPE: trim, upper-case, map common variants; lift literals out so view is reusable.
  CASE
    WHEN d.EMPLOYEE_TYPE IS NULL OR TRIM(d.EMPLOYEE_TYPE) = '' THEN NULL
    WHEN UPPER(TRIM(d.EMPLOYEE_TYPE)) IN ('FACULTY', 'PROFESSOR', 'INSTRUCTOR', 'LECTURER') THEN 'FACULTY'
    WHEN UPPER(TRIM(d.EMPLOYEE_TYPE)) IN ('STAFF', 'ADMINISTRATIVE', 'ADMIN', 'ADMINISTRATOR', 'NON-FACULTY') THEN 'STAFF'
    WHEN UPPER(TRIM(d.EMPLOYEE_TYPE)) IN ('STUDENT', 'UNDERGRAD', 'GRAD', 'GRADUATE STUDENT') THEN 'STUDENT'
    WHEN UPPER(TRIM(d.EMPLOYEE_TYPE)) IN ('RESEARCHER', 'RESEARCH STAFF', 'POSTDOC', 'POSTDOCS') THEN 'RESEARCH'
    WHEN UPPER(TRIM(d.EMPLOYEE_TYPE)) IN ('VISITING', 'VISITOR', 'AFFILIATE') THEN 'VISITOR'
    WHEN UPPER(TRIM(d.EMPLOYEE_TYPE)) IN ('EMERITUS') THEN 'EMERITUS'
    ELSE UPPER(TRIM(d.EMPLOYEE_TYPE))
  END AS EMPLOYEE_TYPE,
  d.FULL_NAME AS FULL_NAME
FROM drupal_employee_directory d
employee_directory_keyed.description: Canonical employee directory rows keyed by MIT_ID exposing EMPLOYEE_TYPE and NAME fields. Clean/canonicalize EMPLOYEE_TYPE values (no question-specific literals).

course_offering_cohort_with_materials_fl.name: course_offering_cohort_with_materials_flag
course_offering_cohort_with_materials_fl.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  c.`SECTION_ID` AS `SECTION_ID`,
  c.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  c.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` AS `MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`,
  c.`TERM_CODE` AS `TERM_CODE`,
  c.`IS_OFFERED_THIS_YEAR` AS `IS_OFFERED_THIS_YEAR`,
  c.`IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM` AS `IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM`,
  c.`IS_OFFERED_SPRING_TERM` AS `IS_OFFERED_SPRING_TERM`,
  c.`IS_OFFERED_SUMMER_TERM` AS `IS_OFFERED_SUMMER_TERM`,
  c.`IS_OFFERED_IAP` AS `IS_OFFERED_IAP`,
  c.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME` AS `RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME`,
  c.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID` AS `RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID`,
  c.`MEET_PLACE` AS `MEET_PLACE`,
  -- Flag: any TIP material records for this term+subject+section
  CASE WHEN EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM `tip_subject_offered` tso
    WHERE tso.`TERM_CODE` = c.`TERM_CODE`
      AND tso.`SUBJECT_ID` = c.`SUBJECT_ID`
      AND (tso.`TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY` IS NOT NULL)
  ) THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END AS `HAS_TIP_MATERIALS`,
  -- Flag: any TIP_DETAIL records referencing this subject_offered (by term+subject) with non-null TIP_MATERIAL_KEY or ISBN
  CASE WHEN EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM `tip_detail` td
    WHERE td.`TERM_CODE` = c.`TERM_CODE`
      AND td.`SUBJECT_ID` = c.`SUBJECT_ID`
      AND (td.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY` IS NOT NULL OR td.`ISBN` IS NOT NULL)
  ) THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END AS `HAS_TIP_DETAIL`,
  -- Flag: any library_reserve_catalog linked via library_reserve_matrl_detail for this offering (term+subject)
  CASE WHEN EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM `library_reserve_matrl_detail` lmd
    WHERE lmd.`TERM_CODE` = c.`TERM_CODE`
      AND lmd.`SUBJECT_ID` = c.`SUBJECT_ID`
      AND lmd.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` IS NOT NULL
  ) THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END AS `HAS_LIBRARY_RESERVES`,
  -- Aggregate summary: concatenated distinct TIP material titles (if any) for reporting (may be null/empty)
  (SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT tm.`TITLE` SEPARATOR '; ')
   FROM `tip_detail` td2
   JOIN `tip_material` tm ON tm.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY` = td2.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY`
   WHERE td2.`TERM_CODE` = c.`TERM_CODE`
     AND td2.`SUBJECT_ID` = c.`SUBJECT_ID`
  ) AS `TIP_MATERIAL_TITLES`
FROM `course_catalog_subject_offered` c
-- No additional joins required for the specified output columns; TIP/library checks done via correlated subqueries

iap_session_row_level.name: iap_session_row_level
iap_session_row_level.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY AS SESSION_ID,
  c.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY AS CATEGORY_ID,
  -- ATTENDANCE in iap_subject_detail is a stored attendee count may be non-numeric; try to cast to signed, leave NULL if not castable
  CASE
    WHEN s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN d.ATTENDANCE REGEXP '^[0-9]+$' THEN CAST(d.ATTENDANCE AS SIGNED)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS ATTENDEE_COUNT,
  d.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  sp.SPONSOR_NAME AS SPONSOR_NAME,
  s.SESSION_START_TIME AS START_TIME
FROM iap_subject_session s
-- session -> session_detail relation: both share IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY; bring in detail for TERM_CODE and ATTENDANCE and CATEGORY key and sponsor key
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_detail d
  ON d.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
-- bring category to get CATEGORY_ID (IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY) and ensure exact source of category id
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_category c
  ON c.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY = d.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY
-- bring sponsor to get SPONSOR_NAME from exact table
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_sponsor sp
  ON sp.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY = d.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY
iap_session_row_level.description: One row per IAP session, normalized/cleaned session-level attributes needed for aggregation: session id, category id, attendee count (as integer, nulls left for later coalesce), term code, sponsor name, start time.

iap_session_term_lookup.name: iap_session_term_lookup

SELECT
  at.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  at.TERM_START_DATE AS TERM_START_DATE,
  at.TERM_END_DATE AS TERM_END_DATE
FROM academic_terms AS at
JOIN (
  -- distinct TERM_CODE values present in sessions via subject detail -> session relation
  SELECT DISTINCT sd.TERM_CODE
  FROM iap_subject_detail AS sd
  JOIN iap_subject_session AS ss
    ON sd.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = ss.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
  JOIN iap_subject_category AS cat
    ON sd.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY = cat.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY
  -- note: literals (filters) should be applied by consumers of this view
) AS codes
  ON at.TERM_CODE = codes.TERM_CODE
iap_session_term_lookup.description: Lookup linking session TERM_CODE to canonical term attributes (term start/end/date) from academic_terms, one row per session TERM_CODE; used to compute min/max TERM_CODE or other term-based ranges for sessions.

mailing_list_member_counts_by_list.name: mailing_list_member_counts_by_list
mailing_list_member_counts_by_list.body_sql:
SELECT
  dcc.SECTION_ID AS SECTION_ID,
  dcc.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID,
  ded.MIT_ID AS MIT_ID,
  ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY AS MOIRA_LIST_KEY,
  COUNT(mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER) AS total_members,
  SUM(CASE WHEN mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS members_with_mit_id,
  -- counts by department (raw member counts); department taken from moira_list_detail.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER (raw string)
  -- provide a concatenated summary of counts by department using GROUP_CONCAT: "dept:count" pairs
  GROUP_CONCAT(CONCAT_WS(':', COALESCE(mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID, 'UNKNOWN'), dept_counts) SEPARATOR ';') AS members_by_mit_id_and_count
FROM drupal_course_catalog dcc
-- join to moira_list to identify the mailing list (assume SECTION_ID corresponds to MOIRA_LIST_NAME; lift literals out by leaving mapping implicit)
LEFT JOIN moira_list ml
  ON ml.MOIRA_LIST_NAME = dcc.SECTION_ID
LEFT JOIN moira_list_detail mld
  ON mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
-- join to drupal_employee_directory to get MIT_ID matching the required column; match on MIT id from moira_list_detail if present
LEFT JOIN drupal_employee_directory ded
  ON ded.MIT_ID = mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID
-- aggregate helper: compute counts per moira list and member mit id
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    MOIRA_LIST_KEY,
    MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID,
    COUNT(*) AS dept_counts
  FROM moira_list_detail
  GROUP BY MOIRA_LIST_KEY, MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID
) t_counts
  ON t_counts.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
  AND t_counts.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID = mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID
WHERE dcc.SECTION_ID IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY dcc.SECTION_ID, dcc.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID, ded.MIT_ID, ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY

semantic_filters.none: no intrinsic literal filters; keep general

mailing_list_member_counts_by_list.description: Per-mailing-list aggregated counts: total members and members by department code (raw counts). Grain is one row per mailing list identifier.

moira_subscriber_membership.name: moira_subscriber_membership
moira_subscriber_membership.body_sql:
SELECT
  ml.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS list_name,
  mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID AS subscriber_id,
  ml.IS_PUBLIC AS is_public,
  -- derive subscriber_type from whether we have a MIT_ID vs plain member string; keep original columns only:
  -- there's no explicit subscriber_type column in source, expose a best-effort classification while still
  -- including the raw member column for traceability. The view requires subscriber_type, so we produce it
  -- here using MEMBER vs MIT_ID presence.
  CASE
    WHEN mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID) <> '' THEN 'mit_id'
    WHEN mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER) <> '' THEN 'member_string'
    ELSE 'unknown'
  END AS subscriber_type,
  mld.LAST_UPDATE_DATE AS subscribed_at,
  -- carry through keys to preserve joinability / grain
  mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY AS list_id,
  mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER AS subscriber_raw
FROM
  moira_list ml
JOIN
  moira_list_detail mld
    ON ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
moira_subscriber_membership.description: One row per MOIRA mailing-list subscriber membership (a subscriber on a specific list). Exposes subscriber identifier, list name, subscriber metadata needed to exclude system accounts, and any membership timestamps/flags if available.

list_member_with_person_affiliation.name: list_member_with_person_affiliation
list_member_with_person_affiliation.body_sql:
SELECT
  ml.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS `list_name`,
  mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID AS `subscriber_id`,
  ml.IS_PUBLIC AS `is_public`,
  fa.AFFILIATION_ROLE AS `affiliation_role`,
  fa.ORG_UNIT_NAME AS `org_unit_name`
FROM moira_list ml
JOIN moira_list_detail mld
  ON mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
LEFT JOIN (
  -- SIS affiliations: assumed to be represented by fac_organization joined to moira members by org key or member id.
  -- Preserve affiliation columns from a base "sis_affiliations" source by constructing from available tables.
  -- Carry through keys so rows remain joinable.
  SELECT
    fod.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID AS MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID,
    fo.ORGANIZATION_KEY AS ORG_KEY,
    fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME AS ORG_UNIT_NAME,
    fo.ORGANIZATION AS AFFILIATION_ROLE -- using ORGANIZATION as role placeholder from fac_organization
  FROM moira_list_detail fod
  LEFT JOIN fac_organization fo
    ON fo.ORGANIZATION_KEY = fod.MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY
  GROUP BY fod.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID, fo.ORGANIZATION_KEY, fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME, fo.ORGANIZATION
) fa
  ON fa.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID = mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID
list_member_with_person_affiliation.description: Denormalized view joining MOIRA list memberships to SIS person affiliations so each membership row includes the person's SIS role and department/org. Enables counting total subscribers per list and counting students per department per list.

building_floor_area_floor_level.name: building_floor_area_floor_level
building_floor_area_floor_level.body_sql:
SELECT
  `fac_floor`.`FLOOR_KEY` AS `FLOOR_KEY`,
  `fac_floor`.`FLOOR` AS `FLOOR`,
  `fac_floor`.`BUILDING_KEY` AS `BUILDING_KEY`,
  COALESCE(`fac_floor`.`EXT_GROSS_AREA`, 0) AS `EXT_GROSS_AREA`,
  COALESCE(`fac_floor`.`ASSIGNABLE_AREA`, 0) AS `ASSIGNABLE_AREA`,
  `fclt_floor`.`FCLT_FLOOR_KEY` AS `FCLT_FLOOR_KEY`,
  `fclt_floor`.`FCLT_BUILDING_KEY` AS `FCLT_BUILDING_KEY`,
  COALESCE(`fclt_floor`.`EXT_GROSS_AREA`, 0) AS `FCLT_EXT_GROSS_AREA`,
  COALESCE(`fclt_floor`.`ASSIGNABLE_AREA`, 0) AS `FCLT_ASSIGNABLE_AREA`
FROM `fac_floor`
LEFT JOIN `fclt_floor`
  ON `fac_floor`.`FLOOR_KEY` = `fclt_floor`.`FCLT_FLOOR_KEY`
  AND `fac_floor`.`BUILDING_KEY` = `fclt_floor`.`FCLT_BUILDING_KEY`
building_floor_area_floor_level.description: Normalized floor-level area and counts for each floor row; canonicalize NULL numeric areas/counts to 0 so downstream aggregation can sum safely.

fac_rooms_rowlevel_cohort.name: fac_rooms_rowlevel_cohort
fac_rooms_rowlevel_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- room identifier: use fac_rooms.FAC_ROOM_KEY as the stable room-level key
  `fac_rooms`.`FAC_ROOM_KEY` AS `ROOM_IDENTIFIER`,

  -- room area: pass through stored AREA (no aggregation or casting)
  `fac_rooms`.`AREA` AS `ROOM_AREA`,

  -- major use: use stored MAJOR_USE_DESC from fac_rooms
  `fac_rooms`.`MAJOR_USE_DESC` AS `MAJOR_USE`,

  -- occupying organization: use stored ORGANIZATION_NAME from fac_rooms
  `fac_rooms`.`ORGANIZATION_NAME` AS `OCCUPYING_ORGANIZATION`,

  -- building key: pass through stored BUILDING_KEY from fac_rooms
  `fac_rooms`.`BUILDING_KEY` AS `BUILDING_KEY`

FROM `fac_rooms`

WHERE
  -- filter out rows lacking a room identifier: require FAC_ROOM_KEY to be non-null and non-empty
  `fac_rooms`.`FAC_ROOM_KEY` IS NOT NULL
  AND `fac_rooms`.`FAC_ROOM_KEY` <> ''

  -- filter out non-room aggregates: require ROOM to be present (room-level records)
  AND `fac_rooms`.`ROOM` IS NOT NULL
  AND `fac_rooms`.`ROOM` <> ''
fac_rooms_rowlevel_cohort.description: One-row-per-room cohort for rooms (room-level records) with basic identifiers and raw measures. Filters out rows lacking a room identifier and non-room aggregates; keeps room area as-is for later numeric casting and aggregation.

fac_rooms_area_and_occupancy_normalized.name: fac_rooms_area_and_occupancy_normalized
fac_rooms_area_and_occupancy_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  TRIM(fr.ROOM) AS ROOM_IDENTIFIER,
  -- Coerce ROOM_AREA to numeric: prefer stored AREA in fac_rooms; if null fall back to 0.0
  CAST(fr.AREA AS DECIMAL(18,3)) AS ROOM_AREA,
  fr.MAJOR_USE_DESC AS MAJOR_USE,
  fr.ORGANIZATION_NAME AS OCCUPYING_ORGANIZATION,
  fr.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  -- Grain/id: carry through stored room key (use FAC_ROOM_KEY if present, else FCLT_ROOM_KEY if joined)
  fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY AS ROOM_ID
FROM fac_rooms AS fr
fac_rooms_area_and_occupancy_normalized.description: Normalized projection of room-level key fields with ROOM_AREA cast/coerced to numeric, canonicalized ROOM_IDENTIFIER (trimmed) and canonical occupying organization. Does not aggregate; one row per room (same grain). Useful for numeric aggregations and joins.

rooms_counts_by_major_use_and_area_by_or.name: rooms_counts_by_major_use_and_area_by_organization

building_address_counts.name: building_address_counts

SELECT

  b.BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS AS BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS,

  + (CASE WHEN b.BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(b.BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS) <> '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
  ) AS address_field_count
FROM buildings b
building_address_counts.description: Counts of address fields present per building. Since no separate address table exists in this schema chunk, count non-null/non-empty BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS and BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS for each building (result 0..2).

reserved_materials_records.name: reserved_materials_records
reserved_materials_records.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.SECTION_ID AS SECTION_ID,
  c.SUBJECT_CODE AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  c.SUBJECT_NUMBER AS SUBJECT_NUMBER,
  c.SUBJECT_TITLE AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  c.IS_OFFERED_THIS_YEAR AS IS_OFFERED_THIS_YEAR,
  c.HASS_ATTRIBUTE AS HASS_ATTRIBUTE,
  c.ACADEMIC_YEAR AS ACADEMIC_YEAR,
  c.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  c.MEET_PLACE AS MEET_PLACE,
  c.MEET_TIME AS MEET_TIME
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered c
JOIN library_reserve_matrl_detail r
  ON r.TERM_CODE = c.TERM_CODE
  AND r.SUBJECT_ID = c.SUBJECT_ID
JOIN library_reserve_catalog rc
  ON rc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY = r.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY
JOIN library_material_status ms
  ON ms.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = r.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY
WHERE ms.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS LIKE CONCAT('%', 'reserve', '%')
   OR ms.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_CODE LIKE CONCAT('%', 'reserve', '%')
reserved_materials_records.description: Row-level cohort of records that represent 'reserved materials' according to a reservation/status column; exposes identifiers, title, publication year, status, and associated course identifiers for downstream aggregations.

course_title_and_publication_year.name: course_title_and_publication_year
course_title_and_publication_year.body_sql:
SELECT
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID` AS SECTION_ID,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_CODE` AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_NUMBER` AS SUBJECT_NUMBER,
  -- canonicalize title: trim whitespace and collapse internal repeated spaces to single space
  TRIM(REGEXP_REPLACE(COALESCE(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_TITLE`, ''), '\\s+', ' ')) AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` AS ACADEMIC_YEAR,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`HASS_ATTRIBUTE` AS HASS_ATTRIBUTE,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`HGN_CODE` AS HGN_CODE,
  -- raw title length (number of characters after canonicalization)
  CHAR_LENGTH(TRIM(REGEXP_REPLACE(COALESCE(`course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_TITLE`, ''), '\\s+', ' '))) AS RAW_TITLE_LENGTH
FROM `course_catalog_subject_offered`
course_title_and_publication_year.description: Projection and cleaning of course/catalog records to canonicalize title and publication year fields and compute raw title length. Keeps one row per section and preserves status/course identifiers for grouping.

reserved_materials_per_publication_year.name: reserved_materials_per_publication_year
reserved_materials_per_publication_year.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.ACADEMIC_YEAR AS ACADEMIC_YEAR,
  c.SECTION_ID AS SECTION_ID,
  c.SUBJECT_TITLE AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  c.HGN_CODE AS HGN_CODE,
  c.HASS_ATTRIBUTE AS HASS_ATTRIBUTE,
  -- aggregated measures per publication year (ACADEMIC_YEAR)
  COUNT(rm.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY) AS reserved_material_count,
  -- average title length (characters) from library_reserve_catalog.CATALOG_TITLE
  AVG(CHAR_LENGTH(lrc.CATALOG_TITLE)) AS avg_catalog_title_length,
  -- distinct material status count (from library_material_status.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY via reserve detail)
  COUNT(DISTINCT lms.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY) AS distinct_material_status_count,
  -- distinct course count (distinct SUBJECT_ID from reserve detail)
  COUNT(DISTINCT rm.SUBJECT_ID) AS distinct_course_count
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered c
-- join reserve detail to identify reserved materials and link to catalogs and statuses
LEFT JOIN library_reserve_matrl_detail rm
  ON rm.TERM_CODE = c.TERM_CODE
  AND rm.SUBJECT_ID = c.SUBJECT_ID
LEFT JOIN library_reserve_catalog lrc
  ON lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY = rm.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY
LEFT JOIN library_material_status lms
  ON lms.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = rm.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY
WHERE rm.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  c.ACADEMIC_YEAR,
  c.SECTION_ID,
  c.SUBJECT_TITLE,
  c.HGN_CODE,
  c.HASS_ATTRIBUTE
reserved_materials_per_publication_year.description: Aggregated measures per publication year for records marked as reserved materials: raw counts, average title length, distinct status count, distinct course count. Does not apply sorting so it can be reused.

course_offerings_cohort.name: course_offerings_cohort
course_offerings_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY AS OFFERING_ID,
  so.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  so.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  so.MEET_TIME AS TERM_DURATION,
  so.IS_OSE_SUBJECT AS IS_OFFERED_IAP,
  sps.SPONSOR_NAME AS SPONSOR_NAME,
  so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME
FROM subject_offered AS so
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_detail AS iad
  ON iad.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_sponsor AS sps
  ON sps.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY = iad.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY
WHERE
  -- Filter out rows that are clearly not section-level or not real offerings:
  so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY IS NOT NULL
  AND so.TERM_CODE IS NOT NULL
  -- Exclude obvious empty placeholder rows
  AND (so.SUBJECT_ID <> '' OR so.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID <> '')
  -- Offerings should have a section identifier to be an atomic scheduled offering
  AND so.SECTION_ID IS NOT NULL
course_offerings_cohort.description: One-row-per course offering/section (the atomic scheduled offering). Filters limited to remove obviously irrelevant rows; does not assume which column marks IAP — leaves that to question_ops. Exposes keys and common term/subject/sponsor fields for later filtering/aggregation.

sponsor_normalized.name: sponsor_normalized
sponsor_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through an offering identifier so the view is joinable; source table: subject_offered
  subject_offered.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY AS OFFERING_ID,
  -- canonical sponsor name: prefer iap_subject_sponsor.SPONSOR_NAME then subject_offered.OFFER_DEPT_NAME then NULL-normalized empty
  NULLIF(TRIM(
    COALESCE(
      iap_subject_sponsor.SPONSOR_NAME,
      subject_offered.OFFER_DEPT_NAME,
      ''
    )
  ), '') AS SPONSOR_NAME,
  -- responsible faculty name as stored on subject_offered, trimmed and normalized to NULL if empty
  NULLIF(TRIM(subject_offered.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME), '') AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME
FROM subject_offered
-- left join to sponsor table via sponsor key present in iap_subject_detail -> iap_subject_sponsor relationship.
-- subject_offered may relate to iap_subject_detail via SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY -> subject_summary.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY -> iap_subject_detail.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY is not directly joinable in our schema.
-- Best-effort: join subject_offered to iap_subject_detail using SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY = subject_summary.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY via subject_summary if available.
LEFT JOIN subject_summary
  ON subject_offered.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY = subject_summary.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_detail
  ON subject_summary.SUBJECT_SUMMARY_KEY = iap_subject_detail.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_sponsor
  ON iap_subject_detail.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY = iap_subject_sponsor.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY
sponsor_normalized.description: Canonicalized sponsor/person name rows for use when joining/attributing offerings. Normalizes NULL/empty and trims whitespace, provides a single sponsor_name field derived from common sponsor/responsible columns.

SELECT

  END AS BUILDING_COUNTER_NULL_MARK
FROM
  buildings b
buildings_with_counters_normalized.description: Normalized building-level projection that exposes building identifier, name, and a numeric BUILDING_COUNTER; casts BUILDING_COUNTER to integer and marks NULLs explicitly — reusable for any query needing building floor counts or numeric comparisons.

course_catalog_subject_term_instructors.description: One row per subject-term combination from course-catalog-level tables, with canonical per-term instructor fields normalized into a single instructor text column. Includes rows from catalog tables that record instructors at the subject/term level.

drupal_subject_term_offerings.name: drupal_subject_term_offerings
drupal_subject_term_offerings.body_sql:
SELECT
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` AS `EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE`,
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_CODE` AS `SUBJECT_CODE`,
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS `SUBJECT_TITLE`,
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`SECTION_ID` AS `SECTION_ID`,
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME` AS `RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME`
FROM `drupal_course_catalog`
drupal_subject_term_offerings.description: One row per drupal catalog subject-term offering including term code, subject identifiers, subject title, section id, and responsible faculty name (section-level).

student_basic_records.name: student_basic_records
student_basic_records.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.MIT_ID AS MIT_ID,
  d.FULL_NAME AS FULL_NAME,
  d.OFFICE_PHONE AS OFFICE_PHONE,
  c.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  c.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS DEPARTMENT_NAME
FROM drupal_employee_directory d
LEFT JOIN course_catalog_subject_offered c
  ON d.OFFICE_LOCATION = c.MEET_PLACE
student_basic_records.description: One row per student with canonicalized full name and their assigned department identifier and department phone if available. Exposes student identifiers and name fields so downstream aggregations can compute counts and name-length measures.

department_reference.name: department_reference
department_reference.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` AS `DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
  c.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  d.`OFFICE_PHONE` AS `OFFICE_PHONE`
FROM `course_catalog_subject_offered` c
LEFT JOIN `drupal_employee_directory` d
  ON c.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` = d.`HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE`
     OR c.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` = d.`HR_ORG_UNIT_ID`
department_reference.description: One row per department code/name exposing canonical department identifiers and contact phone if present in schema. Normalize department name and phone for joins to student records.

students_assigned_to_departments.name: students_assigned_to_departments
students_assigned_to_departments.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.`MIT_ID`                             AS `MIT_ID`,
  d.`FULL_NAME`                          AS `FULL_NAME`,
  s.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`                    AS `DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
  s.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`                    AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  d.`OFFICE_PHONE`                       AS `OFFICE_PHONE`
FROM
  `drupal_employee_directory` d
JOIN
  `course_catalog_subject_offered` s
    ON s.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` = d.`HR_ORG_UNIT_ID`
WHERE
  d.`MIT_ID` IS NOT NULL
  AND d.`MIT_ID` <> ''
  AND (s.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` IS NOT NULL AND s.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` <> '')
students_assigned_to_departments.description: Denormalized row-level view: one row per student assignment to a department. Joins student records to department info and ensures only students with a non-empty department code are included. Provides student full name and department fields needed for counting and computing max name length.
